$comment: Buildings drawn as low isometric blocks, in the manner of a pictorial estate map. The footprint is drawn twice: once in a shadowed wall tone at its true position, and again in the roof wash shifted up-screen. The band of wall left visible below the roof is what reads as height.
$comment_honesty: The offset is a CONSTANT drawing convention, not a height. NO source building carries a height tag (0 of 1,173), so nothing here claims one - every block is the same depth, which is why it reads as illustration rather than as survey. `height_m` stays null in the data. If real heights ever arrive, this is the layer to replace with fill-extrusion.
$comment_anchor: fill-translate-anchor is viewport, so the blocks always lift towards the top of the screen. The offset is interpolated by zoom so a building looks equally solid at every scale.
label: Buildings

$lift.$comment: Shared by every translated layer so the roof, its wash and its outline move together. Change it in one place. Values are [x, y] screen pixels; y is negative because translate's y axis points down, and the roof lifts up.

layers.$comment: Walls: the footprint at its true position, in shadow.
Roof: the same footprint lifted up-screen.
Pigment over the roof, so it granulates like the rest of the sheet.
The crisp ink edge that makes a footprint read at any zoom.
